Phaeochromocytoma. Pharmacological management of phaeochromocytoma (p.1179) is principally achieved by alpha- adrenergic blockade and tachycardia may subsequently be con- trolled by cautious addition of a beta blocker. There have also been some reports1-4 of the use of nifedipine to treat cardiovascu- lar symptoms in adults and children with phaeochromocytoma. 1. Serfas D, et al. Although beta2 agonists or magnesium are the drugs that have been most commonly used as tocolytics to postpone premature labour (p.2003), there is increasing interest in calcium-channel blockers such as nifedipine, either given alone or added to other tocolytics, as first-line drugs.
